record.paper: Separation choosability and dense bipartite induced subgraphs

dossier_meta.paper: Separation choosability and dense bipartite induced subgraphs
dossier_meta.statement_text: There is a function $x_1(d)$ that satisfies $x_1(d) \to \infty$ as $d \to \infty$ such that $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G) \geq x_1(d)$ for any graph $G$ with minimum degree $d$.
dossier_meta.context_text: The authors prove Theorem 1.2 that separation choosability grows logarithmically in minimum degree for bipartite graphs, and ask whether the bipartiteness assumption can be dropped. The difficulty is that a bad list assignment with maximum separation on a graph does not necessarily retain maximum separation when edges are added, so the standard bipartite-subgraph reduction used for ordinary choosability fails.
